 kept     journal          on disk below /var/log/journal. A panic stops journald before it writes
                           the last lines, and lines below priority CRIT reach the disk every
                           SyncIntervalSec=5min
 kept     pstore-backend   efi_pstore is the persistent store: a panic leaves the end of the kernel
                           log in it
 kept     pstore-archive   systemd-pstore.service is enabled and moves the dumps to
                           /var/lib/systemd/pstore at boot
 kept     pstore-vs-kdump  no crash kernel is loaded: a panic goes to pstore
 info     kdump            no crash kernel is loaded, and efi_pstore keeps the panic text. kdump is
                           a second way to keep it
 none     mce-bootlog      not an x86 host (aarch64): this check is about the machine check banks of
                           x86 processors
 none     mce-print        not an x86 host (aarch64): this check is about the machine check banks of
                           x86 processors
 info     reset-kind       aarch64 with a firmware error source: a fatal firmware error panics the
                           kernel, and with panic=0 the host stays down until a watchdog or the BMC
                           restarts it. With panic=N the kernel restarts N seconds after the panic,
                           and the next boot reads what pstore kept
 none     bert             the firmware provides no BERT table
 none     erst-mce         not an x86 host (aarch64): this check is about the machine check banks of
                           x86 processors
 kept     console          a serial console (ttyAMA0): the BMC's serial log or a console server
                           keeps the last lines
 kept     rasdaemon        rasdaemon.service is enabled and records to
